snapshot.source_crosscheck: The parent agent independently confirmed all 2544 source-file hashes and sizes match D:\liuzhe\Desktop\code\Vibe-Trading.
snapshot.inspection: Read-only source inspection. No dependency installation, service startup, broker access, or credential reads.

reading_notes: Entrypoints are classified as HTTP API, Agent tool, CLI slash command, or library primitive. A module's existence is not treated as proof that it is wired into a user workflow.
Statuses such as source-supported describe code only; no live market, brokerage, or account behavior was exercised in this audit.
Evidence paths are relative to the locked upstream source root inside the archive. Line numbers refer to that exact snapshot.

entrypoints.description: Each user message creates an Attempt and runs the AgentLoop with the session transcript, tool registry, and selected skills.

persistent_objects.name: Session
persistent_objects.storage: Filesystem tree: sessions/{session_id}/session.json, messages.jsonl, attempts/{attempt_id}/attempt.json, and partial response checkpoints.
persistent_objects.relations: Session.last_attempt_id links the latest Attempt; Message.linked_attempt_id and attempt parent IDs preserve turn grouping; terminal messages carry run_id and tool trail metadata when available.

persistent_objects.name: Attempt
persistent_objects.storage: Per-attempt JSON; state includes pending/running/waiting_user/completed/failed/cancelled/interrupted.
persistent_objects.relations: An attempt belongs to one session and can point to a backtest run directory.

capabilities.flow: A general research conversation can discover data through registered Agent tools, save files or reports, and end in a transcript with status, tool calls, and artifact links. SSE streams messages, attempts, and terminal events. On restart, unresolved attempts are reconciled as interrupted; the last user message is not automatically resent.
limits: This is a general Agent runtime, not a stock-only workflow. Data source and tool availability depend on provider configuration, installed optional packages, and per-session tool registry.
POST /sessions/{id}/messages returns an accepted message/attempt ID before the analysis completes; callers must follow events or read the attempt.

actions: swarm tool can list presets/runs and start, cancel, retry, or resume runs.

persistent_objects.name: SwarmRun, task DAG, events, artifacts, and agent inboxes
persistent_objects.storage: One run directory containing run.json, append-only events.jsonl, tasks/, inboxes/, artifacts/.
persistent_objects.relations: Tasks belong to a run, task dependencies encode a DAG, artifacts/inbox messages attach to task/worker execution. Resuming creates a new run and reuses only successful upstream task outputs.

capabilities.flow: A preset materializes a multi-agent DAG; a background runtime executes workers, persists per-task outputs, and streams progress. Run and task states are durable. The API retries or resumes failed/cancelled work into a new run.
limits: A preset is a generic team definition; its existence does not prove market data coverage or quality for a specific symbol/window.
An API run start does not carry a universal request_id. Hosted callers need their own durable request/receipt association if a POST outcome is uncertain.

actions: hypothesis list/show/invalidate and other registry commands

persistent_objects.name: Hypothesis
persistent_objects.storage: Atomic JSON list, default ~/.vibe-trading/hypotheses.json; VIBE_TRADING_HYPOTHESES_PATH may override.
persistent_objects.relations: link_backtest stores a run-card path or run directory with optional metrics, validation summary, and notes in the hypothesis record.

capabilities.flow: The registry supports create/update/search and explicit linkage from a hypothesis to a backtest artifact. Status labels include exploring, testing, validated, rejected, and monitoring.
limits: No dedicated hypotheses HTTP route is registered in api_server.py; the durable entry is through Agent tools and CLI.
Linkage is an explicit tool call using paths/summary data, not an automatic foreign-key chain from every session or run.
capabilities.maturity: durable but manually linked research object

actions: alpha_zoo list_alphas/get_alpha/health; alpha_bench and alpha_compare evaluate existing library entries.

persistent_objects.name: Bundled factor definitions and benchmark jobs
persistent_objects.storage: Factor code and metadata are read from the bundled factor registry. HTTP benchmark/compare job state is held in process-local job dictionaries; benchmark output can also be written as an HTML report.
persistent_objects.relations: Bench/compare jobs reference alpha IDs, universe, period, selection, and progress/result; they do not create a user strategy code artifact.

capabilities.flow: Browse bundled factors, inspect source/metadata, benchmark factors, compare selected IDs, read result/progress. This is a factor-research loop, not an interactive strategy-code authoring or execution pipeline.
limits: CSI300 readiness requires both Tushare token configuration and the Tushare dependency. S&P 500 is marked public-data ready; BTC-USDT is rejected for cross-sectional IC because it is one asset.
Alpha benchmark job state is in memory and can disappear on process restart. Actual data coverage depends on the selected universe provider and its period/history.
The API offers list/get/bench/compare, not a factor registration or source-code mutation endpoint.
capabilities.maturity: connected evaluation for bundled factors; not user-authored strategy lifecycle

persistent_objects.name: Artifact
persistent_objects.storage: SQLite strategy_store.db by default; override path is supported. Related tables hold bench_history, adaptation_bindings, and decay_snapshots.

capabilities.flow: Register a factor/strategy record, attach its source/logic and optional hypothesis/governance fields, update lifecycle, record benchmark history, and scan for decay. Decay scans require at least three usable benchmark observations to classify an artifact.
limits: Model governance metadata is optional for a bare artifact. If any governance fields are supplied, intended_use and limitations are required.

The four-eyes check reports a developer/approver match but explicitly does not block it. The only hard validation transition rule is that APPROVED cannot be reached directly from UNVALIDATED; every other transition is left to caller discretion.
The tools can register descriptions and file paths; they do not themselves generate strategy code or prove a broker-ready strategy.
capabilities.maturity: durable asset lifecycle with partial, caller-driven model governance

persistent_objects.name: strategy_regime_evidence
persistent_objects.storage: SQLite disposable evidence cache, default <runtime-root>/strategy_discovery.db or ~/.vibe-trading/strategy_discovery.db; environment/config override supported.
persistent_objects.grain: One row per strategy_id and market regime, with trades, position size, return/benchmark/excess, Sharpe, drawdown, date ranges, cost breakeven, evidence quality, warnings, provenance run directory, verification date, and regime definition.

persistent_objects.name: Adapted strategy artifact
persistent_objects.storage: Child StrategyStore artifact plus an atomic adaptation binding and a prepared run directory containing config.json and an empty code/ folder.
persistent_objects.relations: Child derives_from parent, starts CREATED/UNVALIDATED, has no inherited run/code attestation; parent evidence must belong to parent and pass freshness/quality gates.

capabilities.flow: Catalog combines Alpha Zoo and SDM records, enriches them with per-regime evidence, queries can require evidence quality, trade count, cost feasibility, Sharpe and non-stale evidence. Evidence refresh consumes explicit run directories/manifest and rebuilds the cache. Adaptation creates a gated child scaffold; the response then instructs a separate skill/code-generation, backtest, and evidence-refresh sequence.
limits: This is not a one-click research-to-verified-strategy workflow. Code generation, backtesting, and evidence refresh are separate actions.
Evidence is a disposable cache, not source of truth. Invalid run entries are skipped; path and state/artifact gates can prevent ingestion.
Adaptation is description-limited: the patch type allows name, universe, and position sizing; parent signal rules are not edited by this function.
capabilities.maturity: evidence workflow is connected; code and backtest remain explicit subsequent steps

actions: backtest_tool runs a supplied run_dir containing config.json and code/signal_engine.py.

persistent_objects.name: run directory
persistent_objects.storage: Runs under the configured Vibe runtime; contains config.json, generated code, state.json, run_card/metrics/positions/curve and other engine artifacts when produced.
persistent_objects.relations: Run IDs identify result views; strategy artifact run_dir and hypothesis run_cards may separately link to this directory. BacktestTool marks success/failure lifecycle state.

capabilities.flow: Code is supplied or generated into a run directory; backtest validates the contract, runs the configured engine, records state and artifacts, and exposes results. Factor/strategy evidence ingestion is a separate tool step.
limits: A working backtest depends on a valid signal_engine.py/config and a loader covering the requested instruments, interval, and date range.
The backtest engine can compute metrics; it does not establish out-of-sample validity, live tradability, or profitability by itself.
capabilities.maturity: connected run execution/result retrieval; code creation and higher-level validation are separate

actions: POST /upload for supported document/data file upload; report download endpoints are separate.

persistent_objects.name: Normalized in-memory trade frame
persistent_objects.storage: The analyzer reads the user-selected CSV/Excel path and computes a result; this tool itself does not save a durable trading account or journal object.
persistent_objects.relations: Parser output supplies normalized trades to profile/behavior calculations or to the separate Shadow extraction tool.

capabilities.flow: Parses Tonghuashun, Eastmoney, Futu, and generic files; profile and behavior analyses are implemented. The strategy_features branch still returns a pending Phase 4c placeholder.
limits: Eastmoney CSV/XLSX parsing is file analysis, not an Eastmoney online account connector.
Strategy extraction is a separate Shadow tool; it is not the output of analyze_trade_journal(analysis_type=strategy).
capabilities.maturity: file-in/file-out analysis; strategy path in this tool remains a placeholder

actions: GET /shadow-reports/{shadow_id}?format=html|pdf; report is fetched by opaque shadow ID.

persistent_objects.name: ShadowProfile
persistent_objects.storage: <runtime-root>/shadow_accounts/{shadow_id}.json; content includes source journal hash, market, date range, profitable/total round trips, profile text, preferred markets, and 3-5 structured rules.
persistent_objects.relations: Rules feed a generated signal engine and backtest config; backtest run outputs/cache live under shadow_runs/{shadow_id}/{currency}; report HTML/PDF under shadow_reports; the report can include scan results.

capabilities.flow: A trade file produces a durable ShadowProfile; the user can run historical replays, render HTML/PDF, and scan current liquid baskets against extracted rules. These are separate explicit tool calls, but the objects link through shadow_id and the report can run a missing backtest itself.
limits: This is simulation/research only and does not place or relay orders.
Markets are grouped by settlement currency; each currency pool starts with full capital. The headline is one comparable currency pool and there is no FX aggregation across pools.
Today's scan examines bounded built-in baskets and price features, not a whole-market screener or continuous live scanner.
Market coverage and report PDF engine availability depend on loaders and optional render packages.
capabilities.maturity: connected four-step shadow workflow; not broker execution

actions: portfolio_summary reads an immutable snapshot; optional target_weights returns a value-only proposal. portfolio_risk_xray computes historical basket risk.

persistent_objects.name: Portfolio snapshot
persistent_objects.storage: SQLite portfolio/portfolio.sqlite3; immutable snapshots plus FX quotes/cache. Settings and connections are separate runtime-root JSON stores.
persistent_objects.relations: Snapshot ties source account rows and positions to snapshot_id, FX rates/as-of, completeness, valuation totals, and normalized combined holdings; Agent analysis can pin an exact snapshot_id.

capabilities.flow: Refresh reads every enabled read-only source, values positions/cash, applies reference FX, records per-source failures, and saves an immutable complete or incomplete snapshot. Risk x-ray consumes a symbol/weight basket; rebalance consumes a pinned snapshot and target weights.
limits: A failed enabled source is omitted from holdings but marks the snapshot incomplete; it is not silently treated as a complete portfolio.
PortfolioService only reads and never places/cancels orders.

Rebalance is proposal_only: requires complete snapshot, fresh FX, priced assets, long-only holdings, and target weights summing to one; returns value changes, no quantity/order/tax/fee/execution price.
Import paths support specific files such as ExtraETF holdings; they do not create online broker access.
capabilities.maturity: connected read-only account aggregation and value-only allocation proposal

actions: GET /api/connections, POST/PUT/DELETE connections, list/select account, set credentials, check connector.

persistent_objects.name: TradingConnection
persistent_objects.storage: Connections and selected portfolio sources are under runtime root; connector credential values are stored in OS vaults or connector-owned OAuth/local-session stores, while the API returns only credential status.
persistent_objects.relations: Connection pins profile/environment/transport and optionally one broker account reference; portfolio settings can enable a read-only eligible connection.

capabilities.flow: The user selects a declared connector profile, creates a connection, supplies its declared credential fields or authorizes its own OAuth/local session, selects an account where needed, then runs a read-only status check and can add portfolio-eligible profiles to the read snapshot.
limits: Portfolio accepts only read-only profiles declaring both account.read and positions.read.

Built-in connectors include IBKR, Robinhood, Tiger, Longbridge, Alpaca, OKX, Binance, Futu, Dhan, Shoonya, Trading212, MT5, eToro, Zerodha, KIS, Upbit, Toss, Scalable, and m.Stock; local plugins can extend the read-only catalog.
No Eastmoney broker connector/profile is present. Eastmoney is an OHLCV market-data loader and a trade-file parser elsewhere in the source, not online ordinary-trading-account access.
capabilities.maturity: read connector lifecycle implemented; actual account behavior requires the provider's own session, credential, and permissions

actions: TradingConnectorTool and remote live order tools call profile-capability-gated service functions for place/cancel/close/modify.

persistent_objects.name: Mandate, consent record, halt flag, live audit chain, runner jobs/counters
persistent_objects.storage: <runtime-root>/live/{broker}/mandate.json, consent records, kill-switch marker, audit.jsonl and audit_chain.jsonl; runner job/budget state is broker-scoped.
persistent_objects.relations: A live order is linked to the active unexpired mandate and consent record; kill switch may block actions or apply configured cancel/flatten behavior. Live audit is separate from research-run traces.

capabilities.flow: Paper and live are separate connector profiles/environment declarations. Live mandate proposals are read-only; only surface-originated explicit consent_ack can commit a mandate. Commit writes a one-use consent-linked, expiring mandate after rechecking broker ceilings. Runner start requires an unexpired mandate and an untripped kill switch.
limits: Paper profiles may expose orders.place without real funds; live order profiles declare orders.place.requires_mandate. Profile semantics are provider-specific: Alpaca separates paper/live hosts; Futu uses local OpenD and a live trade-password unlock; Longbridge paper/live identification is operator-declared and live order placement is not exposed in the cited profile.
This is a real-money capable subsystem; it depends on an explicitly supported broker, its SDK/OAuth/local terminal, account permissions, mandate, and limits.
No Eastmoney ordinary-account adapter exists, so a normal Eastmoney account cannot use this live/paper order workflow in this snapshot.
capabilities.maturity: implemented but requires supported broker environment and explicit approval; unrelated to read-only portfolio

persistent_objects.name: ScheduledResearchJob and per-firing delivery/verdict state
persistent_objects.storage: <runtime-root>/scheduled_research/scheduled_research_jobs.json; proposal JSON is separately persisted with expiry/status.

capabilities.flow: Agent tool proposals do not change jobs; a human must commit or discard. Commit checks proposal freshness and requires the scheduler executor enabled/running. The authenticated REST API also exposes direct create/update/delete paths; direct POST persists a pending job immediately, separate from the Agent proposal approval path. A scheduled firing enqueues an Agent session attempt; completion and report delivery are tracked separately.
limits: Scheduler availability is an environment/configuration dependency; a stored PENDING job does not prove an active executor.
Delivery needs a configured origin/channel target; PDF email requires the configured password and optional renderer.
Job ID is not a general idempotency request ID.
capabilities.maturity: complete scheduled-job lifecycle with human-confirmable Agent proposals and separately available direct API mutation

persistent_objects.name: Goal, criteria, claims, evidence, audit rows
persistent_objects.storage: SQLite goal ledger at runtime-root sessions.db by default; one current goal per session, with evidence linked by goal_id and optionally criterion_id, claim_id, run_id, and tool_call_id.

capabilities.flow: A session can define objective, criteria, risk tier, and budgets; add traceable evidence; then record criterion audit rows and status/recap. Goal progress can be injected into the Agent session context.
limits: The goal layer is research accountability/progress tracking, not broker approval. API explicitly rejects LIVE_TRADING_OR_EXECUTION research goals.
Evidence may refer to artifacts and run directories; references are records, not automatic proof that an artifact is valid or a conclusion correct.
capabilities.maturity: durable goal/evidence/audit workflow attached to a conversation

actions: AgentLoop writes run_manifest.json beside trace.jsonl; manifest hashes system prompt, tool names, and package versions.
Immutable live action records go to audit.jsonl and a tamper-evident hash chain.

persistent_objects.name: PersistentMemoryEntry
persistent_objects.storage: Markdown-like memory files under ~/.vibe-trading/memory by default.
persistent_objects.relations: Entries are explicitly saved/recalled/reinforced; they are not automatically keyed to hypothesis_id, strategy_id, or backtest run.

persistent_objects.name: RunManifest
persistent_objects.storage: run_manifest.json next to a run trace.
persistent_objects.relations: Content-addressed methodology provenance: system prompt hash, skill coverage note, tool set, package versions, optional small extra fields. It does not copy the system prompt.

persistent_objects.name: Live audit record
persistent_objects.storage: Separate append-only live audit and chained audit file rooted under live state.
persistent_objects.relations: Can tie an order/action to mandate and consent record; separate from research memory.

capabilities.flow: There are three distinct records: user-curated cross-session notes, per-run methodology provenance, and compliance-grade live-action audit. The AgentLoop provenance file is actually wired even though the manifest module's older prose still describes future wiring.
limits: No automatic strategy-method memory promotion is present; an Agent/user must explicitly save a note with remember.
The live governance ledger is not a general model approval service. Strategy artifact governance fields and validation statuses live in StrategyStore.
Several native stores use direct Path.home defaults (for example memory and hypotheses), while other stores use runtime-root helpers; do not assume one root setting retargets every subsystem.
capabilities.maturity: explicit memory and run/audit provenance implemented; not an automated performance-learning loop

capabilities.category: model calculations, exports, and prompt playbooks

actions: project_three_statement; build/diff artifacts; export XLSX and one-slide PPTX.

persistent_objects.name: ModelArtifact
persistent_objects.storage: Library returns an in-memory versioned object containing inputs, outputs, assumptions, gaps/warnings, model/schema version, generation time, and deterministic input hash. XLSX/PPTX exporters write only to the caller-supplied path.
persistent_objects.relations: Artifact diff compares versioned model outputs; there is no strategy_store foreign-key or API persistence route for these QuantLib valuation artifacts.

capabilities.flow: The QuantLib modules are deterministic calculation primitives with strict caller-supplied inputs. The CLI slash commands render research instructions and queue them as Agent prompts; they are not wrappers around run_dcf/run_comps. The library's XLSX/PPTX exports are real but caller-driven.
limits: DCF/comps/three-statement functions do not fetch market or financial data themselves and are not registered as dedicated FastAPI valuation endpoints.
CLI playbooks depend on available Agent tools and provider access; missing inputs must be reported as gaps. /memo is a prompt workflow, not a durable memo business object by itself.
Three-statement model has compute and workbook/deck export functions, but no dedicated slash command or HTTP route was found in the mounted API.
XLSX exporters need openpyxl and PPTX export needs python-pptx.
capabilities.maturity: calculation and export primitives are implemented; institutional CLI is prompt-driven, not a structured valuation API workflow

capabilities.flow: Chain retrieval supplies US-listed option contracts; payoff analysis accepts user-specified legs/scenarios and returns payoff/risk/Greeks; Black-Scholes pricing is a computation tool.
limits: Options chain source is Yahoo Finance and supports US underlyings only. These are analysis endpoints, not order-entry endpoints.
No durable options portfolio or saved trade object is created by these routes.

object_operations.evaluation_boundary: The registry does not calculate or approve a hypothesis. Its status is caller-updated; a backtest link stores supplied evidence metadata.
object_operations.archive_boundary: No archive status/action. Rejected is the invalidation state.

operations: bench via run config or recorded evidence
object_operations.evaluation_boundary: Decay scan evaluates persisted bench history and needs at least three usable observations. Evidence query evaluates separately ingested run artifacts. These are distinct measurement paths.
object_operations.archive_boundary: No archive action. Disable marks an artifact inactive; decayed/disabled parents are blocked from adaptation/default recommendations.

operations: update status with criterion audit rows/recap
object_operations.evaluation_boundary: The store checks current goal identity and criterion audit/completion policy; it does not automatically determine whether a trading strategy is valid.
object_operations.archive_boundary: Goal states include superseded/cancelled; there is no standalone archive action. Deleting its session deletes its goals.

object_operations.evaluation_boundary: Manual reinforcement updates memory quality/importance; it is not a computed strategy-performance evaluation and is not automatically linked to run evidence.
object_operations.archive_boundary: Optional lifecycle GC can archive low-importance memory files; automatic delete is disabled in this tier. User-facing tool offers forget, not a named archive action.

object_operations.evaluation_boundary: Attempt status and terminal transcript are the execution record.
object_operations.archive_boundary: SessionStatus contains archived, but the mounted session routes do not expose a session archive action; DELETE removes the session and its goals.

cross_workflow_assessment.name: research to hypothesis to strategy to backtest to evidence
cross_workflow_assessment.finding: Composable, not one-command. Session research and hypothesis tools can capture an idea and explicit run reference. SDM can register a strategy linked to hypothesis_id. Code generation is a skill/Agent action into a run_dir; BacktestTool executes it. Evidence refresh reads run artifacts into a separate disposable cache; strategy discovery queries cached per-regime evidence. The adaptation workflow explicitly returns next steps rather than executing them. remember is an independent user-curated memory tool.
missing_automatic_links: run directory to strategy evidence (requires explicit refresh)

cross_workflow_assessment.name: trade file to rules to Shadow to report to scan
cross_workflow_assessment.finding: The components are connected by journal_path/shadow_id and can be sequenced end to end. The analyzer's strategy mode is still a placeholder, but extract_shadow_strategy independently parses the same supported file formats and persists rules. Backtest, report, and scan are four separate Agent tool actions; rendering a report can run the backtest when no cached result exists. All outputs remain shadow/research-only.

cross_workflow_assessment.name: account to risk to portfolio proposal
cross_workflow_assessment.finding: Read-only connector profiles feed immutable portfolio snapshots. portfolio_summary can pin a snapshot_id; portfolio_risk_xray uses a ticker/weight basket; rebalancing emits value-only proposal rows. There is no connector or route that converts the proposal into orders.

cross_workflow_assessment.name: schedule and approval
cross_workflow_assessment.finding: The Agent tool follows proposal plus human commit/discard; the direct authenticated scheduled-runs REST CRUD is a separate mutation surface and can persist jobs without the proposal step. Live trading has a stronger, separate surface-level explicit consent gate; neither mechanism is model-rank evidence.

market_and_environment_constraints.finding: Backtest loader fallback order for a_share is Tencent, Eastmoney, BaoStock, AKShare, Tushare, Gildata, local. Tencent and Eastmoney are unauthenticated public OHLCV sources; Tushare needs token and package; Gildata needs a commercial token. This is market-data support only.

The snapshot has Eastmoney market-data loading and an Eastmoney transaction-file parser, but no Eastmoney trading profile/connector in the built-in connector registry. A normal Eastmoney account is therefore not an online account, portfolio, or order connection in this snapshot.

Read-only profile eligibility is based on account.read plus positions.read. PortfolioCompatibility explicitly labels native/contract_tested/experimental; experimental profile declaration is not proof of correct valuation. Several connectors need SDKs, local daemons, OAuth, vendor keys, or market-specific permissions.
The alpha readiness route checks token and installed Tushare dependency for CSI300; S&P 500 is labeled public_data; BTC-USDT is a single-asset universe and cannot run cross-sectional IC benchmark.

source_scope_caveats: No API requests, CLI sessions, backtests, web calls, broker logins, installs, or user credentials were accessed.

The code has distinct path conventions: session, portfolio, scheduled, Shadow, and live subsystems use runtime-root paths, while hypotheses, persistent memory, and the strategy store can default directly to Path.home(). Do not assume one path override retargets all stores.

The upstream manifest module contains an older docstring saying loop wiring is future work, but agent/loop.py actually calls _write_run_manifest and writes run_manifest.json. The implementation call site was used as evidence.
